name: Jaunsari
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Satish, U.S. 1972. The phonology and morphology of Jaunsari; also Satish 1990 A linguistic study of Jaunsari. Not online; LSI Vol 9 Pt 4 (read on archive.org) has no Jaunsari accent statement

sources.citation: Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India. 2023. Linguistic Survey of India: Himachal Pradesh. (archive.org PARI.linguistic-survey-of-india---himachal-pradesh)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Jaunsari appears only in the Western Pahari classification lists and in the bibliography (Satish 1990); no Jaunsari sketch (Jaunsari is in Uttarakhand, and no Census LSI Uttarakhand volume exists on archive.org or the Census LSI page).

sources.citation: Bailey, T. Grahame. 1920. Linguistic Studies from the Himalayas, being studies in the grammar of fifteen Himalayan dialects. Asiatic Society Monographs XVIII. London: RAS.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only mention of Jaunsar is geographic ('Immediately to the east of it is the Jaunsar district'); no Jaunsari sketch. Negative control.

sources.citation: Bailey, T. Grahame. 1908. The Languages of the Northern Himalayas, being studies in the grammar of twenty-six Himalayan dialects. Asiatic Society Monographs XII. London: RAS.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Checked because Saxena 2022 cites Bailey for Jaunsari forms: the scanned contains no occurrence of Jaunsar/Jaunsari at all; Jaunsari is not one of the 26 dialects (Glottolog language code list agrees). Negative control.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0, inventory 1731 'Jaunsari (RA)' at https://phoible.org/languages/jaun1243 (RA = Ramaswami 1999 compilation; Glottolog citekey phoible:1731_Satish1990 ties the inventory to Satish 1990)
sources.note: 51-segment inventory; no note on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page jaun1243 and cldf sources.bib (local copy
sources.note: Descriptive refs: Satish 1972, Satish 1990 only; additional Jaunsari-coded refs: Satish 2000, Matthews 2008 (SIL ESR 2008-013, sil_id 50421), Bhatt & Pathak 2014/2015, Grierson 1916. Classification note cites Hendriksen 1976/1979/1986/1987 for subgrouping (Himachali studies, not Jaunsari descriptions).

sources.citation: Shodhganga (INFLIBNET) records matching 'Jaunsari' (133 hits; e.g. handles 10603/301457, 349651, 375748, 394521, 432387, 4533, 541958, 557978, 634387, 709854) — any post-2000 Indian PhD on Jaunsari phonology/grammar (HNB Garhwal, Delhi, Kumaun universities)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: A recent descriptive thesis would be the best modern primary source; the search returned 133 records but the server timed out before any title could be read, so it is unknown whether a linguistic thesis exists among them.
Consonant and vowel tables only; nothing on stress, accent or tone. Its references are the Census 2011, Grierson LSI 9.4 pp. 383-84, Matthews 2008 (SIL entry 9074) and ScriptSource.

sources.citation: Saxena, Anju. 2022. The Linguistic Landscape of the Indian Himalayas: Languages in Kinnaur. Leiden: Brill (open access via OAPEN, handle 20.500.12657/76653).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mentions Jaunsari only in comparative morphosyntax (case markers, pronouns, emphatic clitic, agentive suffix), with data credited to Satish 1990 and Satish 2000; nothing on Jaunsari stress.

sources.citation: Matthews John. 2008. Jaunsari: A Sociolinguistic Survey. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2008-013. Dallas: SIL International. 50 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lexical-similarity, intelligibility, vitality and bilingualism survey with 210-item wordlists from Chakrata, Chapnu and other sites; the wordlists are field transcriptions that 'have not undergone through phonological and grammatical analysis' (p. 36). No mention of stress or accent (a full-text search for stress/accent/syllab: zero relevant hits).

sources.citation: Indian Institute of Advanced Study. 2002. Pahari Bhasha tatha Sahitya (Hindi). Shimla: IIAS. (archive.org pahari-bhasha-tatha-sahitya)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Jaunsari occurs only in classification passages (Grierson's grouping, speaker counts); no Jaunsari description.

sources.citation: Varma, Siddheshwar. 1978. Pahari Language: A Linguistic Analysis. Simla: Indian Institute of Advanced Study. Jaunsari section pp. 47-51.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The Jaunsari sketch is an abridged reprint of LSI IX.iv pp. 383-386 (marked '[LSI pp. 385-386]'); its 'Pronunciation' paragraph repeats Grierson and says nothing about stress; a full-text search for stress/accent over the whole scanned: zero hits.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.) 1916. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX Part IV: Indo-Aryan Family, Central Group: Specimens of the Pahari languages and Gujuri. Calcutta: Superintendent of Government Printing. Jaunsari section pp. 383-400 (Pronunciation p. 385); Western Pahari introduction pp. 371-382.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The 'Pronunciation' paragraph (p. 385) discusses final -a after long vowels, the a/o alternation, chh~s, deaspiration and l-dropping; nothing on accent or stress. a full-text search for stress/accent/stress/tone over the Jaunsari section (the scanned text) and the Western Pahari introduction (lines 30900-31456): zero hits.

sources.citation: Satish, Umadatt Sharma. 1990. A linguistic study of Jaunsari. New Delhi: Creative Publishers. 106 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, HathiTrust search-only; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PK2610.J3 S28 1990)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PK2610.J3 S28 1990
sources.note: The only published grammar (publication of the 1972 Delhi PhD 'The phonology and morphology of Jaunsari'); source of the PHOIBLE inventory; the work most likely to carry a stress statement. HathiTrust holds it search-only; Harvard has a print copy (a scan can be requested through your own library).

sources.citation: Bhatt, Uma & Shekhar Pathak (eds.). 2015. The languages of Uttarakhand. People's Linguistic Survey of India vol. 30(2). New Delhi: Orient Blackswan. lxiii+284 pp. (Hindi ed. 2014, PLSI 30(1))
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Modern survey volume with a Jaunsari chapter written by a local contributor; PLSI chapters usually give a short phonology including a line on stress. Would also supersede Grierson as the modern overview.

sources.citation: Satish, Umadatt Sharma. 2000. Jaunsari: Dictionary and texts. Dehradun: Current Block Works.

sources.citation: Ramaswami, N. 1999. Common Linguistic Features in Indian Languages: Phonetics. Mysore: Central Institute of Indian Languages. (PHOIBLE source 'RA'; Jaunsari inventory 1731 compiled from Satish 1990)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Second-hand compilation of Satish 1990's phonology; if it summarises suprasegmentals it would give the Satish stress statement at one remove. Not on the CIIL e-books site.

sources.citation: Satish, Umadatt Sharma. 1972. The phonology and morphology of Jaunsari. PhD thesis, University of Delhi. 358 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Full 358-page phonology and morphology, three times the length of the 1990 book; a phonology chapter of this size almost certainly treats stress/suprasegmentals. Not digitised (pre-Shodhganga); OCLC 221338747.

sources.note: The result list loaded once (count and handles only, no titles captured); every subsequent request for result pages or the individual handle records timed out (server overloaded), so I could not tell whether any of the 133 records is a linguistic thesis on Jaunsari.
